transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (CTO - SternWave), Tom Reyes (ML Eng), Priya Anand (Security Lead), Luca Marino (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
SternWave is evaluating Redwood for a production inference path. Primary asks: p95 targets for interactive features (~<250-400ms for short prompts), streaming requirements for multi-turn chat, and how Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private maps to cost and security constraints. Next step: benchmark template and POC scoping.

Topics: p95 targets; streaming token/sec; concurrency & burst sizing; caching (prefix/KV); VPC/KMS/SOC2; rollout path (canary, fallback).

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone — thanks for carving out time. Quick intro from us: I'm Jordan, AE — Samir is our SE and will take the deeper perf questions.
[00:18] Maya (SternWave CTO): Hi, thanks. I'll kick off with our high level: we have a conversational data product embedded in our UI. Roughly 40% of users are interactive, they expect near real-time answers. Our internal target is p95 under 350ms for short bursts — that's aggressive but doable.
[00:35] Tom (ML Eng): To add, typical prompt lengths are 30-80 tokens, but some sessions stream longer multi-turns where we keep KV cache across the session.
[00:48] Samir (Redwood SE): Got it. When you say p95 < 350ms, is that token latency end-to-end or server-side generation time?
[00:55] Maya: End-to-end from click to first token in the UI. We measure client RTT ~40ms, so we need server p95 close to 300ms or less.
[01:10] Jordan: Cool. High-level hosting question — are you leaning Hosted, Dedicated, or Private?
[01:16] Priya (Security): Security is a gating item. We need SOC2 compliance and customer-managed KMS for key control, plus SSO with SCIM/SAML. Data residency: EU only for some datasets.
[01:28] Samir: Those are straightforward. Hosted can meet SOC2 and regional controls; for KMS and strict residency we can propose Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated with VPC peering.
[01:40] Luca (SRE): From ops perspective, we also want predictable scaling during marketing spikes — spikes of ~1.2k concurrent chat sessions, baseline ~200.
[01:51] Tom: Concurrency map: average token/sec per active stream ~45 tokens/sec; bursts see up to 250 tokens/sec across multiplexed requests. We want p95 to hold in those spikes.
[02:05] Samir: That's helpful — gives us a shape. For streaming, Redwood's continuous-batching/runtime tries to keep per-stream latency low while batching to improve tokens/sec economics. For example, single-stream p95 for short prompts on our hosted setup is often 150-300ms depending on model/quantization and sequence length.
[02:23] Jordan: We're going to propose a benchmark plan: you send sample prompts and traffic profile, we'll run token/sec and p95 sims across hosted and dedicated configs and share numbers.
[02:34] Maya: Perfect. A few specifics — do you expose KV/prefix caching? We rely heavily on session history to avoid re-encoding long contexts.
[02:43] Samir: Yes, KV cache is supported. It reduces per-token compute for multi-turns and helps latency for longer sessions. But cache hit rates and prefetching matter — we'll need your session distribution to size it properly.
[02:58] Tom: What about quantized model performance — we run 8-bit quant in prod today for cost. How much p95 delta do you see with int8 vs float16?
[03:07] Samir: Typically int8 can reduce latency slightly and reduce memory footprint allowing higher concurrency, but it is model dependent. For many Llama-family models we've seen 10-25% improvements in tokens/sec with quant, sometimes at minor quality tradeoffs. We'll include quant profiles in the benchmark.
[03:25] Priya: For Private deployment, what's the audit surface? We need logs for every inference and admin action for compliance.
[03:32] Jordan: Private includes customer-managed control plane and audit logs; Dedicated gets audit logs and longer retention as add-on. We'll share our SOC2 report and the audit logging spec.
[03:41] Luca: During spikes, we need graceful degradation — fallback to smaller model or cached summary responses. Does Redwood support automatic fallbacks?
[03:49] Samir: Yes, routing policies can failover to smaller variants or a lower-cost compute tier, and we can do canary rollouts. We can tune fallback to prefer latency SLO over cost or vice versa.
[04:02] Maya: Can you give rough numbers — if our target p95 is 300ms for 30-60 token prompts, what concurrency per GPU or per dedicated instance should we expect?
[04:13] Samir: Rough ballpark: for a mid-sized open model (13B quantized) on an A100-ish profile, assuming 30-60 token prompts and modest batching, you might get 60-100 concurrent streaming sessions per GPU while keeping p95 in the 200-350ms window. For higher concurrency we'd either scale GPUs or push more batching which can increase latency. We'll provide a spreadsheet mapping tokens/sec and p95 for your exact prompt sizes.
[04:38] Tom: And burst sizing — we can tolerate short p95 increases for 90s marketing bursts, but want steady-state SLO maintained. How fast can Redwood scale?
[04:48] Jordan: For Hosted, autoscaling with burst capacity can be minutes; Dedicated gives faster autoscale within reserved pool and smaller variance. Private depends on your infra — we can offer autoscaler patterns but capacity provisioning is customer-managed.
[05:02] Maya: Ok. About token/sec benchmarks — can you simulate multiplexed streams? Our production is multiplexed: single session sometimes sends 3-4 concurrent prompts (background retrieval, summary, final answer).
[05:14] Samir: Yes, we'll simulate multiplexed patterns. We have a load harness that respects interleaving and tokenizer-level timing. We'll test both sustained throughput and spike microbursts.
[05:27] Priya: Regarding encryption, we need in-flight TLS, at-rest with customer KMS, and HSM options for key wrap. Is HSM supported on Private?
[05:36] Jordan: HSM/KMS integrations are available on Private and can be integrated with Dedicated via bring-your-own-KMS patterns. For Hosted we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in many regions. We'll attach the KMS spec.
[05:47] Luca: Any caveat about cold-starts impacting p95 for rare models?
[05:53] Samir: Cold starts can add 100s of ms depending on model size and whether caches are warmed. For production we recommend keeping a pool warmed for critical models or using a small standby capacity to mitigate cold starts.
[06:08] Tom: Could you share a recent token/sec example? Even roughs are fine for dimensioning.
[06:13] Samir: Sure — ballpark: single-stream throughput for a 13B quant model might be 40-80 tokens/sec. With batching (20-40 request batch) you can get aggregate tokens/sec in the low thousands per GPU. Streaming latency typically depends on first token p95 and per-token latency. We'll detail numbers per model in the benchmark.
[06:34] Jordan: We'll put together two scenarios: interactive chat (p95-focused) and bulk inference (throughput-focused) and map hosting-mode recommendations + cost.
[06:43] Maya: How do you instrument p95? We need tracing correlation with our client IDs and token-level timing.
[06:50] Samir: We emit token-level timings and request traces; we also support tracing hooks to attach your correlation IDs. Redwood Console exposes per-route p95 and token breakdowns.
[07:02] Priya: On SSO, we use Okta and SCIM. Can you federate RBAC?
[07:07] Jordan: Yes, SAML/SCIM and role-based access controls are supported. We'll provide the RBAC docs and the SSO setup checklist.
[07:16] Maya: I want to call out a constraint: certain datasets must never leave EU, even for intermediate cache. So if Hosted, we need EU-only routing and no cross-region fallback unless explicitly permitted.
[07:27] Jordan: We can configure regional routing and hard-region policies; fallback routing would be opt-in. We'll mark that in the POC requirements.
[07:36] Luca: For the POC, we'll need to verify p95 under a synthetic replay and a real-world replay against a staging dataset. Can you support both?
[07:44] Samir: Absolutely. We can run hosted synthetic replay, and for Private we can run the same harness inside your network. For Dedicated we'll run inside the dedicated pool.
[07:56] Tom: What about cost modeling? We need per-1M tokens cost and the effect of batching and caching.
[08:02] Jordan: We'll provide a cost workbook showing per-token cost across hosting modes, and sensitivity to batching/cache hit rate. We'll also show ops cost differences for Private hosting.
[08:15] Priya: Any constraints about logging PII and redaction?
[08:20] Samir: We have redaction options and configurable log retention. For Private you can route logs to your SIEM, and for Hosted we can limit logs and provide redaction at the application layer. We'll include our logging controls doc.
[08:33] Maya: Great. Let's align on timeline: we want a POC in 3 weeks, production in 3 months if POC validates.
[08:41] Jordan: That timeline is reasonable. Immediate action: you share sample prompts + traffic profile — we'll return a benchmark deck and suggested hosting mode.
[08:49] Tom: Any recommended models for balancing latency and quality?
[08:53] Samir: We'll recommend a primary model and a smaller fallback variant. For your prompt sizes and latency target, a quantized 13B or a tuned 7B-highperf might be a good combo — we'll include quality-vs-latency curves.
[09:09] Maya: One last thing — do you charge extra for longer audit log retention or higher observability retention?
[09:15] Jordan: Yes, longer retention and enterprise observability are add-ons. We'll surface pricing in the workbook.
[09:22] Samir: Ok going into the middle of the call we'll look at some quick calibration questions — what percent of sessions are multi-turn beyond 10 messages?
[09:30] Tom: Around 18% are long sessions. Most sessions are under 5 messages.
[09:36] Samir: That distribution helps with KV cache sizing.
[09:40] [10:00] (brief pause while screenshare and whiteboard are arranged)
[10:15] Samir: I'm drawing a sizing diagram — baseline concurrent active sessions 200, spike 1.2k, long sessions 18%. For that shape, one recommended starting point is a small dedicated pool with autoscale + burst on hosted for overflow during spikes. That gives predictable p95 while controlling cost.
[10:38] Maya: Could you run a sample run hitting the dedicated pool and show p95 histogram?
[10:44] Samir: We'll run that in the POC. We'll also do a replay with your multiplexing pattern to verify first-token p95.
[10:53] Jordan: Summarizing next steps again — we'll send benchmark template, attach SOC2 and KMS/HSM docs, and propose a 2-hour POC scoping.
[11:04] Priya: We'll gather the data residency matrix and KMS contacts and share.
[11:09] Maya: Sounds good. If POC passes, we prefer Dedicated with VPC peering and BYOK for keys.
[11:18] Jordan: Noted. We'll prioritize a Dedicated config in the cost workbook and show private option too.
[11:26] Luca: One operational ask — can Redwood preserve warm caches across deploys or node restarts?
[11:33] Samir: We support cache warm-up strategies and sticky routing to reduce cache churn; for Private you can tune persistence. We'll document cache warm policies.
[11:45] Tom: Great. Any blockers?
[11:48] Priya: None beyond docs and the KMS contacts.
[11:53] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by EOD with the template and scheduling links.
[11:59] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.

Recap & Actions (auto):
- Jordan to send benchmark guide + pricing workbook + SOC2/KMS docs.
- Samir to prepare throughput sims for our prompt set; run multiplexed replay in POC.
- SternWave to provide prompts, traffic profile, residency constraints, KMS contact.

End of transcript.
